recommended_action: Run 'cass index' to refresh the index

recommended_commands.purpose: Index newly discovered sessions without a full rebuild.
recommended_commands.run_when: Run when the index is stale or pending.sessions is nonzero.

recommended_commands.purpose: Confirm the refresh cleared the readiness blocker.
recommended_commands.success_signal: healthy=true or recommended_commands changes to the next blocker

search_completeness.impact: search covers all known conversations; nothing is quarantined

root_cause.summary: no evidence signals pointed at any root-cause family

index.reason: lexical index is older than the stale threshold

semantic.summary: semantic backfill is in progress for the current database
semantic.hint: Run 'cass index --semantic' to finish backfilling current semantic assets; search will use lexical fallback until then.

starter_workflows.name: cold-start
starter_workflows.intent: Discover readiness, exact next command, docs, schemas, workflows, and recoveries from zero context.
starter_workflows.parse_contract: Parse status, healthy, initialized, next_command, recommended_commands[], discovery, starter_workflows[], and mistake_recoveries[].
starter_workflows.note: Use triage first when you do not know whether the archive is initialized; use capabilities/introspect for static API binding.

starter_workflows.name: api-discovery
starter_workflows.intent: Discover the static CLI contract for typed clients and prompt construction.
starter_workflows.parse_contract: Parse workflows, commands, global_flags, exit_codes, env_vars, limits, and response_schemas.
starter_workflows.note: Capabilities is static self-description; triage is the read-only runtime preflight.

starter_workflows.name: health-preflight
starter_workflows.intent: Check whether search is ready before issuing queries.
starter_workflows.parse_contract: Branch on healthy, status, fallback_mode, and recommended_action.
starter_workflows.note: Do not hand-delete index assets; index/doctor are the recovery surfaces.

starter_workflows.name: bounded-search
starter_workflows.intent: Search sessions without flooding the caller's token budget.
starter_workflows.note: Prefer an explicit --limit in automation; limit 0 intentionally means unbounded.

starter_workflows.name: answer-pack
starter_workflows.intent: Build a deterministic cited handoff bundle for another agent.
starter_workflows.parse_contract: Parse evidence[], warnings[], privacy, freshness, health, and omitted[].
starter_workflows.note: Use pack when the downstream consumer needs citations rather than raw search hits.

starter_workflows.name: session-drilldown
starter_workflows.intent: Move from a hit to surrounding conversation context.
starter_workflows.parse_contract: Parse path, line_number, message, surrounding messages, and resume command output.
starter_workflows.note: Use source_path and line_number from search hits; do not infer file formats by hand.

starter_workflows.name: semantic-models
starter_workflows.parse_contract: Parse installed, available, cache_dir, verification status, and err.kind.
starter_workflows.note: Models are opt-in; lexical fallback is valid while the model is absent.

mistake_recoveries.behavior: Levenshtein command recovery corrects the top-level subcommand typo.
Single-dash long global flags are normalized to double-dash form.
Long flags are lowercased when the lowercase spelling is known.
The legacy flag-shaped spelling is normalized into the robot-docs subcommand.
Non-command robot-docs topic shorthands such as commands, schemas, examples, env, paths, exit-codes, and guide route to robot-docs instead of search.
Bare key=value arguments are promoted to known long flags.
robot-docs is already machine-readable; redundant robot/json flags are removed and the guide topic is used by default.
Structured help requests route to the agent guide instead of clap's human help path.
Structured help for robot-docs topics routes directly to the matching robot-docs topic.
Structured command help routes to the machine-readable command reference while plain --help remains native clap help.
ready is accepted as the one-shot agent triage alias.
preflight is accepted as the one-shot agent triage alias.
A top-level structured-output request defaults to read-only agent triage instead of launching the TUI or failing usage.
A top-level robot-mode request defaults to read-only agent triage.
A leading structured-output flag is moved after the robot-capable subcommand.
A leading robot-mode flag is canonicalized to the subcommand's JSON output flag.
A leading data-dir override is moved onto the data-dir-aware subcommand.
A named query option is converted to the required positional query for agent-facing commands.
Short and familiar query aliases such as --q, --text, and --pattern are converted to the required positional query.
Adjacent bare words after search/pack are folded into the query positional before filters are parsed.
Answer/handoff/bundle/evidence aliases route cited-handoff intent to the answer-pack command instead of implicit search.
Question/RC prompt aliases route answer intent to pack, so pack-only evidence flags do not get misparsed as search flags.
Reversed HTML export spellings such as html-export, html_export, and exporthtml route to the self-contained HTML export command.
Current-session shorthands route to session discovery instead of being treated as a search query.
The sessions command accepts current as a positional shorthand for the --current flag.
A bare robot query with pack-only flags is treated as answer-pack intent instead of implicit search.
An explicit structured-output search with pack-only flags is treated as answer-pack intent instead of failing on search-only parsing.
Unquoted top-level words in robot mode are folded into an implicit search query unless they look like a subcommand typo.
A bare query=<value> assignment is converted to the required positional query.
A named path option is converted to the required positional path for drill-down commands.
A grep-style path:line argument is split into the positional path plus --line.
A bare line=<value> assignment is converted to the drill-down --line option.
Search-result field names such as line_number/line-number are accepted as drill-down line aliases.
Search-result field bundles can be pasted directly into follow-up drill-down commands.
Familiar structured-output spellings are converted to cass's robot-format flag on robot-capable commands.
Output-format aliases such as --output json and --output-format json are converted to cass's robot-format flag on robot-capable commands.
A leading structured-output format request is moved onto the robot-capable subcommand.
A common result-count alias is converted to the canonical limit flag.
Snake_case long flags are normalized to kebab-case before alias recovery runs.
A bare result-count assignment is converted to the canonical limit flag.

mistake_recoveries.wrong: cass search auth agent=codex days=7 fields=minimal --json
mistake_recoveries.behavior: Known bare filter assignments are converted to canonical long flags.
Familiar time-window assignments are converted to canonical since/until filters.
Familiar time-window alias flags are converted to canonical since/until filters.
Provider/tool/connector filter aliases are converted to the canonical agent filter.

mistake_recoveries.wrong: cass search auth provider codex limit 5 last 7d --json
mistake_recoveries.behavior: Bare filter key/value pairs after a query are converted before remaining words are folded into the query.
A query placed after leading search/pack filters is moved back to the required query positional.
A familiar short result-count spelling is converted to the canonical limit flag.
